nodes.summary: Two sets $E$ and $F$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ are congruent when some isometry of the plane onto itself maps $E$ onto $F$.
nodes.title: Congruent plane sets

nodes.summary: The countably additive reading of Problem 169: there is a function `μ`, defined for all plane sets, equal on congruent sets, countably additive, extending the Caratheodory linear measure (read as Lebesgue volume on measurable sets), with values in `[0, +∞]` (automatic for `ENNReal`).
nodes.title: Problem of a congruence-invariant countably additive plane measure

nodes.summary: A function $\mu$ that assigns to every subset of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ a value in $[0, \infty]$ is congruence invariant when $\mu(E) = \mu(F)$ for all congruent plane sets $E$ and $F$.
nodes.title: Congruence-invariant set functions on the plane

nodes.summary: `μ` is countably additive on pairwise-disjoint families. This is the countably-additive reading of "additive" in Problem 169; the typescript does not say whether finite or countable additivity is meant.
nodes.title: Countably additive set function

nodes.summary: The countably additive reading is false in ZFC. Sketch: let `V₀ ⊆ [0,1]` meet each `ℚ`-coset of `ℝ` exactly once (Vitali selector) and put `V = V₀ × [0,1]`. Enumerating `ℚ ∩ [-1,1]` as `(qₙ)`, the translates `Tₙ = V + (qₙ, 0)` are pairwise disjoint, each congruent to `V`, so all have the same mass `c = μ V`. Their union contains the unit square `Q = [0,1] × [0,1]` and lies in the strip `[-1,2] × [0,1]` of volume 3,…
nodes.title: No countably additive congruence-invariant measure on all plane sets
